fields.options:
Help

This app lets you configure and manage AI service connections for your Frappe/ERPNext system. It provides a flexible way to integrate with various AI providers like Claude and Perplexity, enabling AI-powered workflows and automation throughout your application.

What You Can Do

  • Configure multiple AI services (Claude, Perplexity, and more) with different authentication methods.
  • Set up secure authentication using Bearer tokens, API keys, or basic auth.
  • Define custom system prompts and user prompts for consistent AI interactions.
  • Set a default service per service type for automatic selection.
  • Add custom headers for specialized API requirements.
  • Test connections to ensure your AI services are working properly.
  • Enable/disable services without deleting them to maintain configuration history.

How to Fill This Form

  1. Service Type: Choose the AI provider (Claude, Perplexity, or custom).
  2. Base URL: Enter the API endpoint URL for your AI service (required).
  3. Authentication: Select the auth type and provide credentials:
    • None: For services that don't require authentication
    • Bearer: Enter your Bearer token
    • API Key: Specify header name (default: x-api-key) and your API key value
    • Basic: Provide username and password for basic authentication
  4. Model Name: Specify the AI model to use (e.g., claude-3-sonnet-20240229).
  5. Custom Headers: Add any additional HTTP headers your service requires.
  6. System Prompt: Define the base instructions for the AI service. (Jinja Support)
  7. User Prompt: Set default user-facing prompts for this service. (Jinja Support)
  8. Default Service: Check this to make this the default for its service type.
  9. Enabled: Keep checked to activate this service, uncheck to disable temporarily.
  10. Test Connection: Use the "Test Connection" button to verify your setup works.

Important Notes

  • Only one default service is allowed per service type (Claude, Perplexity, etc.).
  • You cannot delete the last active service of any type - add another first.
  • API keys and passwords are encrypted for security.
  • Use the ping function to test basic connectivity to your service.
  • Custom headers marked as sensitive will be encrypted in storage.
